- When sentiment is strongly positive (≥0.8) and forecast shows a sharp drop, adjust downward bias by 2–5% to avoid overcorrection.  
- When sentiment is strongly negative (≤-0.3) and forecast is rising, reduce forecast peak by 3–7% to prevent overshoot after spikes.  
- If recent 3–5 day mean is rising and forecast is flat or falling, add 1–3% upward bias to capture momentum.  
- If forecast consistently underestimates true values in early days of 30d horizon, apply 1–2% upward adjustment for lagged mean reversion.  
- When sentiment is mixed (±0.3–0.6) and forecast is volatile, smooth transitions by averaging 2–3 prior values to reduce noise.  
- If true outcome exceeds forecast by >3% for 2+ consecutive days, apply 1–2% downward correction to prevent over-optimistic trend continuation.
